newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sees meat export growth to Russia - AMLC.
newsitem.headline: Australia sees meat export growth to Russia - AMLC.

text.p: Australian meat exports to Russia looked set to increase as reduced European Union meat subsidies improve Australia's competitiveness in the market, Australian Meat and Livestock Corp manager international sheepmeat programmes Rick Capel said on Thursday.

Australian product was currently disadvantaged in terms of price and market accessibility but the drop in subsidies had opened the door, particularly for Australian beef and veal products, he said in a statement.

Russia held the potential for continued growth in Australian meat exports because of Russian concern about rising European prices and threats to continuity and supply because of BSE disease and food safety concerns, Capel said.
Australia exported 10,984 tonnes of meat to Russia in the eleven months to the end of May, up by one-third on the same period last year.
